tasks.spec:
You are reviewing a rebuilt text-message appointment-recall pathway against the signed design map it was derived from. You are REPORT-ONLY. Your output is a verdict, not a rewrite.

BOUNDARY. Everything is staged in ./sources/ in your current task directory. NEVER modify any staged file. NEVER run git. NEVER commit. NEVER call a network endpoint. NEVER load skills, call MCP tools or Apps, or capture notes to any external memory. The ONLY file you create is ./review.json.

WHAT IS STAGED:
- state-procedure-map.md — THE CONTRACT and your yardstick. Eight patient states, five actions each with three outcomes, nine patient replies, nine numbered rules. Read it first.
- v22_graph.json — the generated graph. 22 nodes, 37 edges.
- build_v22_recall_map.py — the generator.
- validate_v22.py — the validator the builder wrote for its own output.
- test_v22_scenarios.py — its 20-test suite.
- v20_sanitized.json — the previous live graph, for comparison.

CONTEXT ON WHAT IS ALREADY MECHANICALLY PROVEN, so you do not waste effort re-proving it. An orchestrator-owned gate confirmed: all 22 required node ids exist with no banned duplicates; n_identity is the only start; every one of the seven silent steps has a != complement and no verify node puts that complement on a booking node; every comparison value is a string literal, zero exceptions; n_faq is global with auto-return and every other global is not; e_timeout is not global and is wired from exactly the three waiting states; no node attaches a tool; n_search maps all eight slot fields; the offer prompt carries start times and no end times and names the timezone; nothing claims a suppression; the confirmation node cannot re-enter booking; the generator is byte-for-byte deterministic. The builder's own validator and its 20 tests pass.

YOUR JOB is what a mechanical gate cannot do.

Hunt specifically for:
- A rule on the map that the graph satisfies literally but violates in spirit.
- A global trigger that can fire when it should not, or that shadows another. Read every globalLabel against every other one and against the real words a patient texts. There are seven globals now; the pairs most likely to collide are the known-question answerer against the office handoff, and the decline exit against the opt-out exit.
- Any path where a patient could be told an appointment is booked when it is not, or where a booking payload could carry a value the gateway did not return.
- Any prompt instruction ambiguous enough that a language model under load would plausibly do the wrong thing, especially around selecting an opening and rendering times for display.
- Anything on the MAP ITSELF that is now visibly wrong or that creates a worse outcome than the defect it replaced. This is the most valuable thing you can find. The map is signed but it is not sacred.
- Anything the test suite claims to cover but does not actually prove.

WRITE ./review.json AS A SINGLE JSON OBJECT WITH EXACTLY THESE KEYS:

  schema_version      string, exactly "mott-v22-review.v1"
  verdict             "APPROVE" or "REVISE"
  checked_dimensions  array of {name, what_you_checked, evidence, result}. Cover at least these areas, naming the rule number where it applies: the failure-exit rule R1, one-state-one-node R2, no model-produced booking values R3, waiting exits and the timeout R4, confirmation gating R5, the message copy R6, the FAQ auto-return R7, the no-false-suppression rule R8, and the string-literal rule R9. what_you_checked must be at least 40 characters of what you actually examined.
  findings            array of {id, severity, locus, evidence, why}. severity is block, high, medium or low. locus names the exact file, node id or edge. evidence must quote real staged text of at least 20 characters, copied character for character. why is at least 40 characters. APPROVE must carry no block or high findings; REVISE must carry at least one.
  residual_risks      array of strings, non-empty. What stays uncomfortable even if you approve.

GROUNDING. An automated validator checks every quote against the staged files. A quote that does not appear verbatim fails the task. Copy real text; never paraphrase inside a quote.

HARD RULES. Do not approve to be agreeable and do not demand revision to look rigorous; the verdict follows the evidence. If the map is wrong, say so. Output valid JSON only in ./review.json, no prose, no code fences.
tasks.verified: the review covers all nine map rules, its verdict is consistent with its own finding severities, at least five quotes appear verbatim in the staged build, and it discloses residual risk
